expected_answer: A company that is not a small company pays company income tax at 30% of its total profits (NTA Section 56(b)).
must_not: states a rate other than 30% for a company that is not small
states that a medium-sized company pays a lower rate such as 20%
rationale: Section 56(b) gives the rate for any company other than a small company; the definition marks which companies are small.

expected_answer: A company with aggregate turnover of ₦20,000,000,000 or more in the year falls under the minimum effective tax rate rule (NTA Section 57(2)(b)).
Where its effective tax rate is below 15%, it must recompute and pay additional tax that brings its effective tax rate to 15% (NTA Section 57(1)).
must_not: states a minimum rate other than 15%
states that the rule applies only to members of multinational groups
rationale: Section 57(2)(b) brings a company with turnover of ₦20 billion and above within the rule; 57(1) sets the 15% floor.

expected_answer: Where two or more companies carry on a trade or business together in a partnership or joint venture in Nigeria, the income or profit is a source of profits and each company's share is taxed separately (NTA Section 11(1)).
must_not: states that the joint venture itself is taxed as one separate taxpayer
rationale: Section 11(1) answers directly.

expected_answer: Expenses wholly and exclusively incurred in producing the income are deductible, including salary, wages or other remuneration paid to employees (NTA Section 20(1)(c)(i)).
must_not: states that salaries paid to staff are not deductible
rationale: Section 20(1)(c)(i) lists employee remuneration among allowed deductions.

expected_answer: No deduction is allowed for an expense on which VAT was due under the Act but was not charged (NTA Section 21(p)).
must_not: states that the expense remains deductible
rationale: Section 21(p) answers; the 21(a)-(o) chunk holds the opening words that make the list non-deductible.

expected_answer: Gains on disposal of shares in a Nigerian company are not chargeable gains where the disposal proceeds in aggregate are less than ₦150,000,000 and the gain does not exceed ₦10,000,000 in any 12 consecutive months (NTA Section 34(1)(a)(i)).
With proceeds of ₦80 million and a gain of ₦5 million, and no other disposals in the 12 months, the gain falls within that exemption (NTA Section 34(1)(a)(i)).
must_not: states that the ₦5 million gain is taxable
states thresholds other than ₦150,000,000 proceeds and ₦10,000,000 gain
rationale: The proviso to Section 34(1)(a) sets both thresholds; the question's figures are under both.

expected_answer: A loss is deducted as far as possible from the assessable profits of the first year of assessment after the loss year, and then from later years until it is fully recouped (NTA Section 27(5)(c)).
A loss can only be deducted from the trade or business in which it was incurred (NTA Section 27(5)(b)).
must_not: states a fixed time limit on carrying the loss forward
states that the loss can be carried back to earlier years
rationale: Section 27(5)(b)-(c) gives the carry-forward rule and its limit to the same trade.

expected_answer: A taxable supply is treated as made when an invoice or receipt is issued, the goods are delivered or made available, or payment is due or received, whichever happens first (NTA Section 147(1)).
must_not: states that the supply takes place only when payment is received
states that the supply takes place only when the invoice is issued
rationale: Section 147(1) uses the earliest of the three events.

expected_answer: A VAT invoice must show the supplier's tax ID, an invoice number, the supplier's name and address, the supplier's incorporation or business registration number, the date of supply, the purchaser's name, the gross amount, and the VAT charged and the rate (NTA Section 153(1)).
Invoices must be numbered in sequence (NTA Section 153(1)).
must_not: states that a VAT invoice is only needed once payment is made
rationale: Section 153(1) lists the contents; 153(2) says the invoice is issued whether or not payment is made.

expected_answer: Federal, State and Local Governments and their Ministries, Departments and Agencies must collect or withhold VAT on taxable supplies made to them and remit it to the Service (NTA Section 155(1)(a)).
VAT withheld must be remitted by the 14th day of the month after the transaction, or as the Service prescribes (NTA Section 155(4)).
must_not: states that a state government agency does not withhold VAT
rationale: Section 155(1)(a) names state government agencies; 155(4) gives the remittance date.

expected_answer: Where a business, or a part capable of separate operation, is transferred as a going concern and the purchaser uses the assets in the same kind of business, the transfer is not treated as a supply for VAT, provided the purchaser is registered or registrable (NTA Section 190(7)).
Section 190 applies to the sale or transfer of a trade or business carried on in Nigeria (NTA Section 157).
must_not: states that VAT is charged on the sale of the going concern without any condition
rationale: Section 190(7) gives the going-concern rule and its conditions; Section 157 applies Section 190 to a business sold out.

expected_answer: Income of companies engaged in agricultural businesses, including crop production, is exempt for the first five years from commencement of business (NTA Section 163(1)(p)).
must_not: states an exemption period other than five years
rationale: Section 163(1)(p) answers; the Thirteenth Schedule lists crop production.

expected_answer: Profits of a co-operative society registered under a co-operative law are exempt, except profits or gains from a trade or business it carries on (NTA Section 163(1)(a)(ii)).
must_not: states that all profits of a cooperative are exempt, including trading profits
rationale: The exemption in 163(1)(a)(ii) carries its own trade-or-business exception.

expected_answer: The total deduction for donations in a year cannot exceed 10% of the company's profit before tax for that year (NTA Section 164(5)).

The deduction is for donations to qualifying funds, bodies or institutions in Nigeria, such as public funds and religious, charitable, educational or scientific institutions (NTA Section 164(1), (3)).
must_not: states a cap other than 10% of profit before tax
states the cap as a share of turnover
rationale: Section 164(5) sets the cap; 164(3) lists the recipients.

expected_answer: The research and development deduction for a year cannot exceed 5% of the company's turnover for that year (NTA Section 165(2)).
must_not: states the cap as a share of profit
states a cap other than 5%
rationale: Section 165(2) answers.

expected_answer: A small company has gross turnover of ₦50,000,000 or less a year and total fixed assets not exceeding ₦250,000,000 (NTA Section 202, "small company").
A business providing professional services is not classified as a small company (NTA Section 202, "small company").
must_not: gives the Administration Act's ₦100,000,000 small business limit as the small company test
rationale: The definition gives both limits and the professional services exclusion.

expected_answer: The year of assessment is the government tax year, 1 January to 31 December (NTA Section 202, "year of assessment").
must_not: states a tax year that starts in a month other than January
rationale: The definition answers; the Administration Act's calendar-year definition states the same months.

expected_answer: An exported service is a service rendered by a taxable person to a non-resident person outside Nigeria, wherever the service is rendered (NTA Section 202, "exported service").
A service rendered to the Nigerian permanent establishment of a non-resident person does not qualify as an exported service (NTA Section 202, "exported service").
must_not: states that the service to the Nigerian branch counts as an exported service
rationale: The proviso in the definition answers: a Nigerian branch is a permanent establishment.

expected_answer: Charging and collection of VAT on petroleum products, LPG and other listed gas items starts on the date the Minister indicates by order in the Official Gazette, and may be suspended (NTA Eleventh Schedule, paragraph 1).
VAT is not collected on those items unless the Minister, by gazetted order, specifies the date of collection (NTA Section 186(2)).
Petroleum products include premium motor spirit and locally produced liquefied petroleum gas (NTA Eleventh Schedule, paragraph 3).
must_not: states that VAT at 7.5% is charged on petrol and cooking gas as a settled rule
states a date on which VAT collection on these items began
rationale: The Eleventh Schedule and Section 186(2) together answer; paragraph 3 confirms petrol and LPG are covered.

expected_answer: The Thirteenth Schedule lists crop production, livestock raising and breeding, livestock processing, forestry (rubber and acacia plantations), dairy product manufacture and cocoa processing (NTA Thirteenth Schedule).
Income of companies in these agricultural businesses is exempt for the first five years from commencement (NTA Section 163(1)(p)).
must_not: lists as exempt an activity that is not in the Schedule or Section 163(1)(p)
rationale: The Schedule's table lists the activities; Section 163(1)(p) is the exemption it serves.

expected_answer: A taxable person must notify the relevant tax authority within 30 days of a change in its particulars (NTAA Section 9(1)).
Changes include the location of business and the registered address (NTAA Section 9(2)(a)).
must_not: states a notice period other than 30 days
rationale: Section 9(1)-(2) answers.

expected_answer: Books and records must be kept for not less than six years after the year of assessment to which the income relates (NTAA Section 31(5)).
must_not: states a period other than six years
rationale: Section 31(5) answers.

expected_answer: The monthly VAT return requirement does not apply to a small business (NTAA Section 22(4)).
A small business has gross turnover of ₦100,000,000 or less a year and total fixed assets below ₦250,000,000, and a professional services business is not one (NTAA Section 147, "small business").
A small business may opt out of the exemption by written notice to the Service (NTAA Section 22(5)).
must_not: applies the ₦50,000,000 small company limit as the test for the VAT return exemption
rationale: Section 22(4) gives the exemption; the Administration Act definition sets who is a small business.

expected_answer: Where a taxable person has not delivered a return and the relevant tax authority considers it liable, the authority may determine the tax due to the best of its judgement and assess it (NTAA Section 35(1)).
That assessment does not affect any other liability for failing to deliver the return (NTAA Section 35(2)).
must_not: states that the tax office cannot assess tax without a return
rationale: Section 35(1)-(2) answers.

expected_answer: The relevant tax authority must respond to the objection within 90 days, otherwise the taxpayer's objection is upheld (NTAA Section 41(6)).
must_not: states that the taxpayer must go to court because the authority did not respond
states a response period other than 90 days
rationale: Section 41(6) answers.

expected_answer: A sum equal to 10% of the tax payable is added to tax not paid within the prescribed period (NTAA Section 65(1)(a)).
For naira remittances the tax also carries interest at the Central Bank of Nigeria monetary policy rate plus a spread set by the Minister, from the due date until payment (NTAA Section 65(1)(b)).
must_not: gives a numeric interest rate that the text does not state
rationale: Section 65(1)(a)-(b) gives both charges; Section 49(5) says unpaid balances attract interest and penalties.

expected_answer: A person who withholds tax and fails to remit it by the 21st day of the following month must pay the amount withheld, an administrative penalty of 10% a year of that amount, and interest at the Central Bank of Nigeria monetary policy rate (NTAA Section 107(1)).
must_not: gives the 40% penalty for failing to deduct as the penalty for late remittance
rationale: Section 107(1) answers. Administration Act Section 22(8) exempts a small business granted the Section 22(4) exemption from Section 107; the question gives no facts pointing to that, so an answer that omits the exception still counts as correct (it is not an omitted proviso that changes the answer), and an answer that mentions it is also correct.

expected_answer: Where a taxable person changes its accounting date, the basis period for the relevant year runs from the day after the previous basis period to the new accounting date, and later years use the new accounting period (NTA Section 23(1)).
The taxable person must notify the relevant tax authority not later than 30 days before the usual due date for filing its income tax returns (NTA Section 23(2)).
must_not: describes section 23 as being about a subject other than a change of accounting date
rationale: Section 23 has two subsections, both summarised.

expected_answer: Section 190 sets the rules that apply when trades or businesses are restructured (NTA Section 190(1)).

On a merger, no new trade is deemed to start, chargeable gains rules do not apply to transferred assets, and unutilised capital allowances and losses pass to the surviving business (NTA Section 190(1)(a)).
On a sale or transfer that ends the trade, the cessation rules apply and unutilised capital allowances, losses and taxes deducted at source do not pass to the new business (NTA Section 190(1)(b)).
The relevant tax authority must be notified of a restructuring before it starts (NTA Section 190(4)).
VAT does not apply to restructuring carried out under the Act, and a qualifying going-concern transfer is not a VAT supply (NTA Section 190(6)-(7)).
must_not: describes section 190 as being about a subject other than business restructuring
rationale: A summary of the whole section; the five points cover its main rules.

expected_answer: Where the relevant tax authority considers that tax assessed has been fully paid or none is due, it must issue a tax clearance certificate within two weeks of the demand, or give reasons for refusing (NTAA Section 72(1)).

Government bodies and commercial banks must demand a tax clearance certificate covering the three years before the current year for listed transactions, such as certificates of occupancy, building plan approvals, government contracts, and import, export and trade licences (NTAA Section 72(2), (4)).
The certificate shows, for the last three years, total profits or chargeable income, tax payable, tax paid and tax outstanding (NTAA Section 72(3)).
must_not: states an issue period other than two weeks
rationale: A summary of Section 72's main rules.
